title: Daily Debrief — Monday, Nov 16, 2026
html:
Daily Debrief · Monday, November 16, 2026 with the new rules and charts; this replaces tonight's earlier debrief.

SPY fell 1.9% to $739.95 and closed under the floor I said would hold. The earlier version of tonight's report saw the PLTR and BA breakdowns and still had one foot on the brake. This one doesn't: two act-now puts for the open, a KO call opened at the close, and how it all lines up for Nvidia on Tuesday night.

The one thing SPY $739.95 is under the $744–745 floor and under its 14, 30 and 50-day. Until it closes back over $745 we lean short, and the plays say so: PLTR and BA puts at the open, not on a retest.

I was wrong about the floor. Sunday's locked call said $744–745 would hold on every close, and it lasted one session. It gets graded Friday.

The open PLTR $180 call is marked $372.50, down $385. Its idea is broken (more below), and Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close with options pricing about a 9% move.

What's going on

What the first version missed, then the forces behind the day

Missed: the act-now puts on PLTR and BA

  • We see: PLTR's 3-day candle (Nov 12–16) closed $160.39, under your 1.382 ($167.37). That's the third of your levels to fail in order: rejected at the 2.0 ($210.51), lost the 1.618 ($183.84), now the 1.382. BA closed $165.22 at a new 52-week low, under its 14, 30, 50 and 200-day, with the 50 under the 200 and the 2-day highs falling ($177.39, $175.16, $171.75).
  • What we did: The earlier report called PLTR's put "ready now" but still framed it around the intraday read, and kept BA waiting for a break of $165. BA missed that line by 22 cents. That is the same habit that cost us the $170 put's run from $562.50 to $870 today.
  • The fix: Both setups are already confirmed on the close. Under the new rules the act-now entry is the next open, with the stop at the nearest real level: a close above $166.09 (today's high) for PLTR, a close above $171 for BA (today's high $170.50). PLTR is 3.45 to 1 to your 1.0, BA 2.3 to 1 to your 1.0. Both pass. The retest is the better price, not the reason to sit out.
  • Wrong if: PLTR closes back over $166.09, or BA over $171.

On your levels and averages, today was a trend day down, not a dip

  • We see: SPY closed under its 14 ($753.77), 30 ($763.00) and 50-day ($763.52), and the 25 ($760.12) has slipped under the 50: a mid-term turn down. The 4-day highs keep falling ($775.64, $765.97, $763.04). PLTR is under every average except the 200 ($153.79). BA is under all of them. NVDA closed $156.14, 81 cents over your 0.5 ($155.33) and $47 under its 200-day.
  • Why it matters: When the averages stack downward and your levels fail in order, a low RSI is weakness, not a discount. The only things still holding are the long-term ones: SPY's 50 over its 200 and the 200-day band at $729.58–732.71.
  • Wrong if: SPY closes back over $745 and the 14-day ($753.77) on a broad day.

The AI trade is being de-risked, not the whole market

  • We see: Nasdaq −2.5%, the chip ETF SMH −5.1%, NVDA −4.1% (−27% in a month), AMD −5.6%, INTC −7.0%. The equal-weight S&P (RSP) fell 1.0%, about half of SPY's 1.9%.
  • Why: When the average stock falls half as much as the index, the selling is in the biggest names. Two AI events are close: Nvidia's first report under interim CEO Colette Kress on Tuesday, and the Anthropic IPO pricing Wednesday night (Yahoo Finance). New US export limits on chips to Southeast Asia hit AMD (Motley Fool). Fairly sure.
  • Wrong if: Nvidia guides strong and SMH closes back over its 14-day (about $502).

Soft data, falling yields, and stocks fell anyway

  • We see: The Empire State survey (New York factories) came in at 7.8 against about 18 expected; new orders fell to 3.0 from 23.2. The 2-year fell 3bp to 4.82%, the 10-year to 5.12% (Newsquawk). WTI fell $2.84 to $85.72 as Hormuz tanker flows recovered.
  • Why: Stocks got the softer data they supposedly wanted and fell anyway. That's a growth worry, not a rates worry. Jefferson still called inflation "the most important consideration," and futures price about 26bp of hikes for Dec 9 (Saxo). Only staples (+0.3%) and utilities (+0.1%) rose; KO made a new high. Moderately sure.
  • Wrong if: Tuesday's retail sales (+0.2% expected) come in hot and yields jump. Then it's rates again.

The market, in one picture

SPY lost its floor and is heading for the 200-day

Dashed = Fib levels, solid red = stop, solid green = trigger or reclaim line, colored lines = 14/30/50/200-day averages, gold dot = last price.

What the chart shows: the bounce off the Nov 5 low ($732.71) stalled under the 30/50-day band near $763 and rolled over. Today's candle closed under the $744.92 line with the 14-day pointing down. The rising 200-day ($729.58) is the next real floor, three dollars under the Nov 5 low.

Bull case: the 200-day band holds and a close back over $745 makes today a flush. Bear case: a close under $729.58 opens $722.22, the 38.2% of the March–October run. What changes my view: a close above $745.

Key levels: $781.62 record high · $771.15 · $757.17 · $744.92 reclaim line · $732.71 Nov 5 low · $729.58 200-day · $722.22.

Your names that matter today

Three decision points, both sides each

Why these: PLTR has an open call with a broken idea and an act-now put, BA has an act-now put, and KO crossed its trigger at the close.

PLTR $160.39 · −4.5% today

  • Your levels: Top to bottom: rejected at your 2.0 ($210.51; record $212.94), lost your 1.618 ($183.84), and the Nov 12–16 3-day candle closed $160.39 under your 1.382 ($167.37). The drawing is on 3-day candles, so this is a break on its own timeframe.
  • Averages: Daily: under the 14 ($173.47) and 30 ($186.89), under the 25/50 ($184.15 / $184.51) and the 100 ($167.20), above only the 200 ($153.79). The 14 is under the 30, the 25 under the 50; the 50 is still over the 200. On the 3-day chart the 50-bar average ($157.56) sits just under price: the first obstacle for the put.
  • Bull case: The 200-day and the Nov 5 low ($152.60–153.79) held last time; RSI 35. A 3-day close back over $167.37 would make this a fake-out.
  • Bear case: Three of your levels failed in order. The next one down is your 1.0 at $140.71.
  • My pick: Bear. The put at the open. The $180 call's idea is broken: I'd sell it at the open rather than wait for its $158 close rule, with Nvidia due.

The 3-day chart is how you drew it. Two closes in a row stalled under the 1.382, and the latest one closed at the low of its range. The 14 and 30 (3-day bars) are turning down; the 50 is the shelf at $157.56.

BA $165.22 · −3.7% today

  • Your levels: Lost your 1.382 ($187.04) in October and never got it back. The next level of yours below is the 1.0 at $151.70. Daily drawing, so daily closes decide.
  • Averages: A strong downtrend by our definition: under the 14 ($172.25), 30 ($180.46), 50 ($187.88) and 200 ($212.99), the 14 under the 30, the 50 under the 200, falling 2-day highs. The 14-day at $172.25 sits right over the $171 stop: the first thing a bounce has to beat.
  • Bull case: RSI 32 after a 13% drop in a month. A close back over $171 traps the late sellers.
  • Bear case: Trend, your ladder and the averages all point down, at a 52-week low.
  • My pick: Bear. Act now at the open; $165 doesn't need to break first. Stretched, so a bounce can come first; the stop is sized for that.

The chart shows a staircase: each bounce since October stopped under the 30-day, and today's candle closed at the bottom of the range. Key levels: $187.04 · $181.5 · $171 stop · $165 · $151.70 target.

KO $99.48 · +0.2% today

  • What happened: New 52-week high at $100.56, closed $99.48, 18 cents over the $99.30 trigger. Intraday it was $99.26, 4 cents under. The new rule: the close decides. So the $100 call is opened at the closing mid, $212.50, noted "entry at close".
  • Averages: A strong uptrend: above the 14 ($95.94), 30 ($93.34), 50 ($91.00) and 200 ($82.80), stacked in order, rising 2-day highs. RSI 74 is strength in an uptrend, not a sell. No drawing of yours yet.
  • Bull case: Staples were one of two green sectors, and KO leads the defensive trade.
  • Bear case: It closed $1.08 off the high: sellers showed up at $100. A close under $97.38 breaks the structure.
  • My pick: Bull, already in. The better price to add is a dip that holds $97.96 (Friday's low).

On the chart, every pullback since September held the 14 or 30-day. Key levels: $105.26 target 2 · $102.64 target 1 · $100.56 high · $99.30 trigger · $97.38 stop.

NVDA $156.14 · −4.1%

Reports Tuesday after the close. It closed 81 cents over your 0.5 ($155.33) on the 2-day chart, after the low ($155.01) poked through. It's under every average; the 200-day is $203.75. No play through the report (IV crush).

XOM $166.87 · −1.6%

Closed two cents under your 2.0 ($166.89) and above the call's $166.50 stop. Not triggered. Tomorrow's close decides break or wick. The put side has no liquid contract (the $165 put's spread is 14%).

Lesson of the day

The close decides, not the cents at the intraday read

KO traded over its $99.30 trigger most of the afternoon, dipped to $99.26 when the intraday read was taken, then closed $99.48. The old rule said the intraday read decides, so the first version of tonight's report left the call out. That's like judging a race at the 90-metre mark.

Our triggers and stops are written as closes, because a close is the price the market agreed to hold overnight. So the rule now reads: if a trigger was within about 0.3% at the intraday read and the close went through it, we open at the closing mid. Four cents is 0.04%. The same goes for stops: a close through a stop closes the play.

What it costs to be strict about it: entered at $99.48, the risk to $97.38 is $2.10 and the reward to $102.64 is $3.16, exactly 1.5 to 1. In dollars, about $78 at the stop against about $200 at target 1.

Plays on deck

Three puts at the open, one call already on

1 · PLTR Dec 18 $150 put

ACT NOW level failure put FAIR

Why now: the 3-day close is under your 1.382, the third of your levels to fail in order, and the AI trade is being sold into Nvidia.

Act now: at the open while PLTR is under $166.09 (≈ $605 at the close). Better price: a bounce into $166–167.37 that closes back under. Exit: a close above $166.09 (today's high).

Targets: your 1.0 $140.71, then your 0.786 $125.77. R:R 3.45 to 1 to target 1 (6.1 to 1 to target 2). Obstacles on the way: the 3-day 50-bar average ($157.56) and the 200-day ($153.79). Worth about $390 at the stop and about $1,433 at target 1 a few days out.

Contract: OI 10,191 · vol 635 · bid/ask $5.95/$6.15 · delta −0.31. IV 58% vs moves 51% → FAIR (1.14). No earnings inside.

2 · BA Dec 18 $165 put

ACT NOW level failure put FAIR

Why now: a strong downtrend on the daily and 2-day, at a 52-week low, under your broken 1.382.

Act now: at the open while BA is under $171. No need to wait for $165. Better price: a failed rally into $179–181.5 (the $170 put is $870 tonight, over the cap, so use the $165). Exit: a close above $171.

Target: your 1.0 $151.70. R:R 2.3 to 1 from $165.22. Stretched (RSI 32), so a bounce can come first; the stop allows for it. Worth about $347 at the stop and about $1,429 at the target a few days out.

Contract: OI 6,302 · vol 1,175 · bid/ask $6.00/$6.25 · delta −0.46. IV 34% vs moves 36% → FAIR (0.93). No earnings inside.

3 · INTC Dec 18 $55 put

ACT NOW breakdown CHEAP

Why now: fell 7.0% to $55.47, under the 78.6% retracement of its Nov 2025 → Jun 2026 run (about $56.31) and under every short and mid-term average. A proposed class action alleges Intel hid weak PC demand (Newsquawk).

Act now: at the open while INTC is under $57.20. Better price: a failed bounce into $57.20–59.66. Exit: a close above $57.20 (today's high).

Target: the Nov 5 low, $51.51. R:R 2.3 to 1. Worth about $338 at the stop and about $610 at the target.

Contract: OI 12,279 · vol 1,455 · bid/ask $4.40/$4.50 · delta −0.51. IV 72% vs moves 98% → CHEAP (0.74; the 60-day includes the Oct 30 gap, so read it as fair-to-cheap).

4 · KO Dec 18 $100 call

OPEN trend continuation FAIR

Entry: $212.50, the Nov 16 closing mid (entry at close). Better price to add: a dip that holds $97.96. Exit: a close below $97.38.

Targets: $102.64, then $105.26. R:R 1.5 to 1 to target 1 (2.75 to 1 to target 2). Worth about $134 at the stop, $415 at target 1 and $617 at target 2.

Contract: OI 4,312 · vol 1,194 · bid/ask $2.05/$2.20 · delta 0.48. IV 21% vs moves 17% → FAIR (1.23, close to expensive). No earnings inside.

The PLTR $180 call: thesis broken It was bought as an uptrend dip with RSI under 40. Your 1.382 broke on a 3-day close, so the idea is gone even though its $158 rule hasn't hit. My exit choice: sell at the open (≈ $372.50, −$385) rather than carry it through Nvidia. Holding to the rule is defensible; just don't widen it.

Skipped today, and why (we count these) HOOD $70 put: most of the move is done after −27% in a month; the entry is a failed bounce into $75.55–81. SPY $710 put: EXPENSIVE (IV 22% vs moves 15%, 1.45). V $440 call: 15% spread, fails liquidity. XOM $165 put: 14% spread. Anything on NVDA through Tuesday's report.

Scorecard: 2 closed, 2-0, +$806.50 · 4 open (KO opened at the close), −$547.50 on paper · 6 watching · early read.

Open book: if HLT, DAL, PLTR and KO all hit their stops, the four calls would be worth about $863 together, about $1,500 under what we paid. Taking all three puts at the open adds about $590 of risk to their stops.

Nvidia Tuesday night

How the plays line up for the report

  • The book: We lean short AI: the PLTR and INTC puts. The PLTR $180 call is the one long AI position, and I'd sell it at the open. BA and KO are mostly outside the AI story, though a big relief rally would pull money out of staples like KO.
  • If Nvidia beats and guides up: Chips and PLTR can gap up Wednesday. The PLTR put's stop is a close above $166.09, 3.6% above tonight. A gap through it means exiting at Wednesday's close: about $390, a loss of about $215. The INTC put at its stop: about $338, a loss of about $107. Together about $322 on the two puts.
  • If it disappoints: The puts have room: PLTR toward the 200-day ($153.79) and then your 1.0 ($140.71); NVDA's own next level is your 0.5 ($155.33), already one dollar away.
  • The habit: Enter the act-now puts Tuesday, not Wednesday. Stops are on closes, so Wednesday's open doesn't stop us out; Wednesday's close does.

Homework for tomorrow

  • On your 3-day PLTR chart, confirm the Nov 12–16 candle closed under your 1.382 ($167.37). Ours closed $160.39. If your candle boundaries differ, go by yours and tell me.
  • On BA's daily, mark the 14-day ($172.25) right over the $171 stop. Watch whether any bounce stalls there.

If Nvidia beats and PLTR opens Wednesday at $165, under the $166.09 stop, do you hold the put to the close or cut it at the open? Write down why before it happens.

Set these alerts

  • PLTR — above $166.09 → the $150 put's stop (a close decides)
  • BA — above $171.00 → the $165 put's stop (a close decides)
  • KO — below $97.38 → the $100 call's stop (a close decides)
  • INTC — above $57.20 → the $55 put's stop
  • SPY — below $729.58 → the 200-day is gone; $722.22 is next

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Fib in action

When a 1.382 stops being a floor

Your PLTR extension: A $118.34, B $188.15, C $70.90, so the swing is B − A = $69.81. Each level is C + ratio × $69.81. 1.382: $70.90 + $96.48 = $167.37. 1.618: $70.90 + $112.95 = $183.84 (the printed values; recomputing lands a cent higher).

In a run, the 1.382 and 1.618 are where moves pause. On the way down they're the floors that get tested. PLTR stalled at the 2.0, lost the 1.618, and now has a 3-day close under the 1.382. When the 1.382 fails, the next line is the 1.0, the "equal move": $70.90 + $69.81 = $140.71. That's the put's target. The stop goes above the failed line at a real level: a close over today's high, $166.09.

Try it: work out your 0.786 ($70.90 + 0.786 × $69.81) and check whether it lines up with the spring 2026 lows on the chart above.

Lesson of the day

The close decides, not the cents at the intraday read

KO traded over its $99.30 trigger most of the afternoon, dipped to $99.26 when the intraday read was taken, then closed $99.48. The old rule said the intraday read decides, so the first version of tonight's report left the call out. That's like judging a race at the 90-metre mark.

Our triggers and stops are written as closes, because a close is the price the market agreed to hold overnight. So the rule now reads: if a trigger was within about 0.3% at the intraday read and the close went through it, we open at the closing mid. Four cents is 0.04%. The same goes for stops: a close through a stop closes the play.

What it costs to be strict about it: entered at $99.48, the risk to $97.38 is $2.10 and the reward to $102.64 is $3.16, exactly 1.5 to 1. In dollars, about $78 at the stop against about $200 at target 1.

Fib in action

When a 1.382 stops being a floor

Your PLTR extension: A $118.34, B $188.15, C $70.90, so the swing is B − A = $69.81. Each level is C + ratio × $69.81. 1.382: $70.90 + $96.48 = $167.37. 1.618: $70.90 + $112.95 = $183.84 (the printed values; recomputing lands a cent higher).

In a run, the 1.382 and 1.618 are where moves pause. On the way down they're the floors that get tested. PLTR stalled at the 2.0, lost the 1.618, and now has a 3-day close under the 1.382. When the 1.382 fails, the next line is the 1.0, the "equal move": $70.90 + $69.81 = $140.71. That's the put's target. The stop goes above the failed line at a real level: a close over today's high, $166.09.
